thread.text:
I built a complete Carrom board game in a single HTML file using vanilla Canvas and zero physics libraries.

• Rigid-disc 2D collision physics (2.2x mass ratio)
• Ghost-ball cushion-bank AI
• Procedural wood lacquer & synthesized WebAudio clacks

Here is how the math works 🧵👇
thread.mediaNote: GIF/Video: Crisp gameplay clip showing a slingshot striker break, carrommen scattering cleanly, and the striker rebounding off cushions with smooth physics.

thread.text:
1/ Disc Collisions & Tunneling:

A carrom striker has 2.2x the mass of a piece. To prevent fast slingshots from tunneling through pieces or rails, the engine runs 8x continuous sub-stepping per frame.

Corner pockets use subtle radial suction wells so edge-glancing shots drop naturally.
thread.mediaNote: Diagram/Video overlay showing disc vector resolution on impact and pocket suction radius.

thread.text:
2/ Ghost-Ball AI & Real-Time Audio Synth:

Hard AI computes ghost-ball pocket vectors and restitution-corrected cushion banks to calculate multi-rail snipes.

Zero MP3 assets: every wood-on-wood collision and pocket drop is synthesized on-the-fly with WebAudio frequency modulation.
thread.mediaNote: Clip of Hard AI executing a clean bank shot into the top-right pocket with audio turned on.

thread.text:
3/ The beauty of zero-dependency architecture:

No npm. No Matter.js/Phaser. No build step. No analytics trackers.

Just pure JavaScript and Canvas rendering in one standalone file. It loads in <0.1s, runs at locked 60 FPS on mobile, and will run forever without breaking.
thread.mediaNote: Screenshot of DevTools showing 0 external network requests and instant DOM load timeline.
